caption:
Adult ADHD: missed, mistaken or misread. Four ways the picture can go wrong.

Getting an ADHD picture right is a known challenge in the research, in both directions. ADHD can be missed for years, particularly when traits are quieter or well covered by coping strategies. It can be recognised as something else first, such as anxiety, low mood or a sleep problem. Things like poor sleep, thyroid conditions or some medicines can look like ADHD. And ADHD often sits alongside other conditions, so finding one does not rule out another.

The Australian ADHD guideline says a diagnosis should not rest on rating scales alone. Over the coming weeks we unpack each of these in our series, ADHD: the full picture.
